gtk+3.0 (3.24.52-3+stereo3d1) unstable; urgency=medium

  * Sparky Stereo OS: a stereo GtkGLArea in GTK 3 (queue row 137, milestone 4,
    stereo3d-gtkglarea-stereo), with the API shape of the edition's GTK 4.
    A stereo area (property stereo) emits its render signal twice for each
    frame, the left view first, and gtk_gl_area_get_current_eye() says which
    view the handler draws. The two views are copied side by side, left
    first, each at the size it was rendered at (stereo-view-width and
    stereo-view-height, the area's own size by default), into one opaque
    picture that goes to the compositor on a surface of its own, declared as
    full side by side stereo content through libstereo-declare: on Wayland a
    subsurface below the window, sized with wp_viewporter to one view, its
    buffer a dma-buf exported from the area's OpenGL context; on X11 a child
    window drawn with the area's own GLX context, or through memory on a
    software renderer (GDK_X11_STEREO_READBACK chooses). The window keeps a
    transparent hole over the area, so its widgets drawn over the area stay
    over it (on X11 when the window has an alpha channel).
  * Depth and colour state: properties format (a GdkMemoryFormat: 8 and 10
    bit, 16 bit, half float, float) and color-state (a GdkColorState). The
    stereo picture keeps the area's depth (XB30, XB48, XB4H) and its colour
    state is described with wp_color_management_v1 on the area's own surface,
    sRGB as gamma 2.2 where the compositor does not list sRGB. GDK gains
    GdkMemoryFormat, GdkColorState and GdkCicpParams under GTK 4's names
    (ITU-T H.273 code points).
  * An area that cannot be shown per eye says so (stereo-shown,
    stereo-error, one log message with the reason) and renders its left view
    alone: no stereo declaration, no dma-buf from the renderer, a format or a
    colour description the compositor does not take, an area partly scrolled
    out or drawn with an opacity below one. An area without stereo, and every
    other widget and window, is unchanged.
  * gtk3-demo: the OpenGL Area demo has a Stereo check button
    (GTK_DEMO_GLAREA_STEREO starts it on) and draws one camera for each eye.
  * testsuite/gtk/glarea: the API, the CICP code points and the honest
    failure on a display without stereo.
  * libgtk-3-0t64 depends on libstereo-declare1 (>= 1.7.0).
